reasons: Both answers critique the two proposals correctly and propose essentially the same layered scheme: long-lived static cards, a listing key versioned by price_ver, and live price and stock from PostgreSQL, with a checkout check and a stampede lock. B adds more practical detail for a three-person team: it names N+1 as a likely cause, warns that Django signals don't fire on bulk_update, over-fetches IDs to handle the in-stock filter, falls back to 'уточните наличие' when stock can't be read, warms caches after import and gives a rough timeline. A's unique strengths (a safety_stock threshold and checking the lag of the stock source) are valuable but slightly narrower, so B wins by a small margin.

B: Lists 'почти 100% попаданий' as a plus for full-page caching while also stating the long tail of filter combinations barely hits cache (internal inconsistency).
